My sweetie found an amazing round trip deal for this winter. We'd fly in one day, spend two full days in Paris, then fly home the 4th day.

We really know nothing about the city. We're not shoppers. We like to walk around and explore new areas (take local transportation to get to new areas, etc.).

Bearing that in mind, are two days enough to get a good sense of the city and get in enough relaxation time as well?

I'm leaning toward going when we can spend more time and take a train to outer areas and get in some countryside too. Especially since it'll be our first trip to Europe together.

I've been all around Ireland and Berlin/Potsdam and London and those trips were at least 5 days each so experience is convincing me 2 days may not be enough at all.
Is two days long enough to enjoy and experience Paris?

Personally, I would say no, it isn't enough time. I was there for 2 days, and it felt frantic trying to cram as much as I possibly could into such a short amount of time. Don't get me wrong, I saw quite a few really cool sites, and it was a great experience, but more time would have been ideal.

This is how I'm leaning. I think he's looking at it from a frugality point of view (which is fine). I mean, $300 round trip each is a phenomenal price but that's not what a trip should be based on (the cheapness to get there). It feels almost criminal to pass up the deal but I think 2 days would be be too stressful/not fulfilling enough.

Part of the problem, as I see it, is when you're in Paris you are actually relatively close to many other amazing things. Versailles is a great example. I had the opportunity to see it while I was in France, and can't imagine not having done so, it's just an absolutely amazing place.

It's definitely a tough decision, as that is a good price. It's just my 2 cents that you might regret not having more time. I know I do.
